paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. A man asks Jesus what good thing he must DO to get eternal life, and he says he has kept the commandments (Matthew 19:20). Then Jesus asks him to let go of his great wealth and follow Him, and the man walks away in sorrow (Matthew 19:22). I think that's the whole lesson sitting right there: he was holding something tighter than he was holding Jesus.

Now watch what happens next. The disciples hear about the camel and the needle and ask, "Who then can be saved?" (Matthew 19:25). Jesus looks at them and says, "With man this is impossible, but with God all things are possible." (Matthew 19:26). So nobody gets in by keeping a perfect list or by having an empty bank account. Salvation is God's work, and that is the best news in the whole passage.

And Peter's question gets a real answer, because Jesus says everyone who has left things behind for the sake of His name will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life (Matthew 19:29). Nobody who follows Him walks away poorer. So here's my question for you, baker: what is the one thing you've got your hands wrapped around? Open them up and follow Him, because He gives back so much more than you could ever hold.
